title: Hari Digma pechay: Characteristics
metaDescription: Hari Digma pechay is an open pollinated (no F1 label) pechay variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Hari Digma pechay is an open pollinated (no F1 label) pechay variety. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Hari Digma pechay is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [pechay variety finder](/crop-varieties/pechay), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [organic fertilizer for pechay](/blog/organic-fertilizer-for-pechay).
Key facts about Hari Digma pechay

rows: Days to harvest, per the seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pechay fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** About 30 days after sowing (Ramgo).
**Fruit:** Leaves: dark green blades on white, juicy stalks.
Ramgo claims tolerance to damping off, soft rot and diamondback moth.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: named right after Black Behi in the IPB UPLB/PCARRD pechay guide reprinted by DA Caraga, Ramgo still sells it on its professional line. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual pechay on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Hari Digma pechay

Pechay is ready in about a month, so it fits small plots and quick cash. Pick a variety that bolts late in the heat and stands rain. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Hari Digma?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
